Microelectronic devices (ICs) require very small levels of voltage and current. It is, therefore, necessary to observe strict precautions to avoid damage or destruction when carrying out testing and troubleshooting procedures..
DISCUSSION

Electrostatic Sensitive Devices are components whose circuits can, by the nature of their construction, be damaged or destroyed by static electricity discharges resulting simply by improper handling procedures...
Each Electrostatic Sensitive Device (ESD), has a different sensitivity to static electricity rating, as depicted in the following table.

Static electricity is electricity at rest and is a phenomenon which everyone has experienced at one time. The effect occurs under certain conditions when the body becomes positively or negatively charged...
The body remains charged until it comes in contact with a substance of the opposite polarity. The effect of the discharge is greater if just the tip of the fingernail slowly touches the substance...

If the potential difference between the substance is great enough, the electrons jumping from the negative charge to the positive charge produce a sudden surge of current (electric shock) across the gap...

The effect is similar to that of a capacitor, the substance and the body are the plates and the air is the dielectric. As a charge discharges into a conductor, the peak voltage and current occur extremely fast; picoseconds or nanoseconds...

The study of the formation of a static charge is called "Triboelectricity" and is derived from the Greek word tribo meaning the action of rubbing. Triboelectricity is electricity generated through rubbing...
Proper precautions and procedures should be followed at all stages of manufacture, storage, transportation, testing, installation, and removal to prevent ESD damage.
Static electricity is generated by two unlike materials rubbed together and then separated. The conductivity of the material determines if the potential equalizes before the separation is complete...

The good conductors (metal) allow the electrons to return to the atom during separation, while in poor conductors (humans, cloth, shoes), the electrons are trapped in the material causing a static charge to remain...

Characteristics of the material, speed of separation, area of contact and relative humidity have an affect on the magnitude of the static charge. Walking across a carpet in 10 percent humidity could build a charge of over 30,000 volts...
A static charge of 30,000 volts would surely damage every component listed in our table.

During storage and transportation safeguarding ESDs are accomplished using special packaging materials wether they are individual devices, card modules or electronic box assemblies.

Individual devices and card modules should be packaged in a quasi-conductive material. The material resistivity should be too high to conduct normal electrical current flow, but low enough to bleed off electrostatic charges. Typical Materials 1. Polyolefin film impregnated carbon. 2. Polyethylene resin impregnate with an anti-static substance ("pink poly").3. Aluminum layer sandwiched by an outer layer of anti-static treated spin-bonded polyolefin and an inner layer of "pink poly".4. Cushion-pack bags made from "pink poly" foam material...
2. Polyethylene resin impregnate with an anti-static substance ("pink poly").
3. Aluminum layer sandwiched by an outer layer of anti-static treated spin-bonded polyolefin and an inner layer of "pink poly".
4. Cushion-pack bags made from "pink poly" foam material.
Printed circuit boards (PCB) and card modules with edge connectors used specially formed strips called "shunts" to keep all the pins at the same potential and protect them against physical damage...
Complete electronic box assemblies use covers and caps made from a conductive material to protect receptacles. Some non-conductive covers sprayed with anti-static conductive film are also used...
Adhesive tape should not be used for sealing a bag as the removal of the tape will generate static electricity.
Static-free packing is of little use if the protected contents are not removed into a static-free environment. Static-free work stations within special handling areas are required for certain ESDs.

This lesson introduces you to the sources of damaging electrostatic discharge, special handling, identification, packaging and principle static control methods used to prevent the damage of electrostatic sensitive devices...
INTRODUCTIONM

A static-free work station consists of conductive work surfaces connected to a grounded conductive floor surface and a stool with a conductive seat cover. The operator wears grounded strap around his/her bare wrist when handling ESDs...

The work station is also equipped with an ionizer to generate positive and negative ions to neutralize any random charges on devices or assemblies. Test specification and assembly direction sheets are contained in anti-static envelopes...
Technicians performing maintenance on equipment containing ESDs outside of special handling areas should follow appropriate precautions and procedures.

Electrical power sources should be isolated and a grounded wrist strap should be worn by the technician prior to removing card modules containing ESDs. Card modules should be immediately placed in an appropriate bag, and identified by a decal...
Technicians removing complete electronic box assemblies do not require grounded wrist straps, however, care should be taken when removing or replacing anti-static connector covers and caps...

The following maintenance practices should be followed to protect ESDs. 1. All repairs should be performed in a dust-free area. 2. Wear anti-static nylon garments when repairing or handling ESDs.3. Ensure personnel and tools are grounded before handling ESDs.4. Use conductive containers with conductive covers during transportation of ESDs.5. After removal from containers, place devices on grounded conductive surfaces.6. Handle devices only when necessary, first grasping the ceramic body or metal can before touching individual leads.
1. All repairs should be performed in a dust-free area.
2. Wear anti-static nylon garments when repairing or handling ESDs.
3. Ensure personnel and tools are grounded before handling ESDs.
4. Use conductive containers with conductive covers during transportation of ESDs.
5. After removal from containers, place devices on grounded conductive surfaces.
6. Handle devices only when necessary, first grasping the ceramic body or metal can before touching individual leads.
Continuity checks should be routinely performed on wrist straps, conductive surfaces, tools, and floor surfaces to ensure continuous static draining.
